title: AI in health care requires evaluation and human oversight
claim: AI for health should be evaluated against ethics, human rights, safety and accountability considerations.
evidence: WHO guidance on ethics and governance of AI for health describes principles and governance considerations for responsible deployment.
strategic_implication: Healthcare AI pilots should have explicit clinical oversight, evaluation criteria and accountability before scaling.

title: Health AI governance must address safety, transparency and accountability
claim: Governance of AI for health should protect autonomy, promote well-being and safety, ensure transparency, foster responsibility and accountability, and promote inclusiveness.
evidence: WHO's guidance sets out principles and governance recommendations for AI used in health.
strategic_implication: Healthcare transformation plans should include risk review, human accountability, validation and an incident response process.

title: Health information exchange needs interoperability standards
source_name: Office of the National Coordinator for Health Information Technology
claim: Interoperability enables health information to be accessed, exchanged and used across systems.
evidence: ONC describes interoperability as a core capability for health information technology and exchange.
strategic_implication: Before building new AI features, healthcare organisations should assess data quality, interoperability and access controls across existing systems.

title: Digital health services should support accessible patient-centred care
claim: Digital health initiatives should support health-system needs and people-centred health services.
evidence: WHO's digital health work frames digital technology as a means to improve health outcomes and service delivery.
strategic_implication: Patient-support automation should be evaluated on accessibility, safe escalation and service quality, not just deflection volume.
